draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Peermade! The name is traditionally linked to Pir Muhammed Waliullah, a Sufi saint said to have meditated in these hills, so Peerumedu means hill of the Peer.
draft.hungryLine: Do what everyone does at Valanjanganam Falls, stop for a cup of tea and watch the water.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Ammachi Kottaram is a 4 min walk, and Valanjanganam Waterfalls is about 17 min away on foot.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Valanjanganam Falls is about 75 ft high and usually wrapped in mist, a perfect spot for a slow tea break.
moodReplies.surprise-me: There was once only a footpath up here, so the British started Aerial Ropeway Ltd, Travancore state's first public limited company.

spots.name: Ammachi Kottaram
spots.detail: 4 min walk · Ruins right around the corner

spots.name: Valanjanganam Waterfalls
spots.detail: 17 min walk · A 75 ft fall, often covered in mist

spots.name: Peeru Hills
spots.detail: 1 km away · Rolling hills close to town

legends.title: Hill of guavas
legends.body: Another local story says the name comes from guava trees, pera, that once grew all over here. The place was called Peramedu, which slowly became Peerumedu.

tips.title: Stop at Valanjanganam.
tips.body: It's right on the Kottayam-Kumily road, an easy place to stretch your legs on a long drive.

tips.title: Carry change for Panchalimedu.
tips.body: The viewpoint charges a small entry fee, listed by Wikivoyage as 10 INR per person.

story.title: Empty hills
story.body: In the 16th century this land was under the Changanacherry kings and nobody lived here.

story.title: Travancore takes over
story.body: The King of Travancore conquered Changanacherry in 1756 and brought these hills under his rule.

story.title: Coffee to tea
story.body: Missionary Henry Baker started coffee plantations here, and under Sri Moolam Thirunal they became tea estates. The Travancore kings also had their summer palace in Kuttikkanam.

story.title: An up-market resort
story.body: Kuttikkanam became a fancy resort, and workers were brought in from across Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

story.title: Estate families
story.body: The descendants of those migrant workers make up most of Kuttikkanam's population today.
